title: Cross-IdP attribute harmonization, failure modes, and RBAC v2 mapping playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a single-source playbook for handling IdP-specific SAML attribute differences, deterministic fallback strategies, and explicit failure-mode handling when mapping IdP assertions to RBAC v2 roles. This ticket covers Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping: canonical attribute/NameID handling, group membership normalization, time skew and assertion expiry heuristics, audit logging correlation (assertion IDs, hashed subjects), and a reproducible test matrix + e2e harness. The goal is to eliminate production ambiguity in user provisioning/mapping and reduce support load from customer SSO mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical fallback order for end-user identity selected and implemented: NameID -> email -> upn -> uid; documented in Confluence and used by RBAC v2 authorizer
Attribute normalization functions implemented for groups, displayName, email, and department with unit tests >= 90% coverage
IdP-specific quirks documented (Okta group limit handling, Azure memberOf nesting, Google domain aliases, Ping assertion format) with mitigation code paths
Audit logs consistently include hashed(subject_identifier), assertion_id, idp_entity_id, and mapping_result (success|partial|failure) for every SAML auth event
Regression test matrix (per-IdP) automated in CI with representative assertions; at least one green run in staging
Playbook contains explicit remediation steps and Slack/Playbook alert text for the support team to handle the 3 most common failure modes
test_plan: Unit tests: attribute_normalizer_test covers 80+ variants of group attributes and NameID formats
Integration: staging SAML flow using local SAML test IdPs for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping (see test harness repo link)
End-to-end: deploy rbac-v2 feature branch to staging, run 50 synthetic logins per IdP with mixed NameID/email/UPN claims, assert mapping stability and correct audit signatures
Chaos: simulate clock drift ±5 minutes and replay old assertion IDs to verify replay detection and logging
Failure injection: remove groups attribute and verify fallback to SCIM/group-sync or label users as 'groups-missing' in audit logs
notes: Decision: We will not accept raw email as the single source of truth when NameID is present; NameID is authoritative if format is persistent or transient with matching subject confirmation

Trade-off: Hashing subject identifiers in audit logs improves privacy but requires consistent salt/versioning; we will include both hashed_subject and idp_entity_id to preserve correlation across systems
Edge-case: Okta can send 'groups' as a JSON string in an attribute; normalizer must attempt JSON parse before splitting on semicolons
Edge-case: Azure AD uses 'http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/groups' but may return nested memberOf; we flatten and prefix with 'aad:' to avoid collision
Performance: group attributes can be large; trim group lists at 500 entries and record truncation in audit log with truncation_count
Security: any fallback that promotes a user to admin role requires an explicit safety gate - deny by default unless admin mapping present in Directory sync or manual assignment
idp_guidance: Okta: prefer attribute 'email' or NameID with Format 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress'. If 'groups' arrives as JSON-encoded string, parse then dedupe; watch for Okta group pagination in SCIM sync (primary mitigation: group-sync job)

Azure AD: accept 'upn' (http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/upn) and 'mail'; 'groups' are often represented via nested memberOf graph responses - use graph API to resolve when group mapping needed for RBAC v2

Google Workspace: NameID often equals primary email; domain aliases can cause dupes—normalize by preserving domain in mapping but surface original assertion in audit logs; groups come via 'memberOf' attribute or via Google Groups API
Ping: Ping installs may use transient NameID or a persistent pairwise NameID; preserve raw NameID in audit logs (hashed storage), and if NameID format is 'transient' prefer email fallback
failure_modes: Missing groups attribute -> RBAC roles not assigned: fallback to directory sync or mark 'groups-missing' and surface in admin console with remediation steps
NameID format mismatch -> ambiguous subject: apply fallback order and record mapping_reason in audit logs; if ambiguity remains, block login to prevent accidental privilege escalation
Clock skew/expired assertion -> reject and instruct IdP to check NTP; allow small skew up to 2 minutes when assertion contains strong anti-replay tokens
Large assertion payloads -> truncation: refuse to map groups beyond threshold and log truncation_count; trigger follow-up ticket to implement group-sync
Assertion replay -> reject and log assertion_id, increment day-of-week metric for replay attempts
observability_and_audit: Audit schema fields to emit: event_time, hashed_subject, idp_entity_id, assertion_id, mapping_result, mapping_reason, truncated_groups_count, raw_nameid_format
Correlation: include SAML Assertion ID as traceable field in span/trace when user action follows an auth event
Retention: keep full SAML assertion for 30 days encrypted with customer_kms for Private deployments; hosted customers: store minimal metadata + hashed ids for 90 days
Alerting: create an alert that fires when mapping_result==failure for >1% of logins over 15m per tenant
Support playbook snippet: copyable Slack text + Confluence runbook pointer to triage common mapping failures
implementation_todos: Add attribute_normalizer module with explicit unit tests for all described edge-cases
Update RBAC v2 authorizer to call normalizer and include mapping_reason in returned binding_response
Add logging hooks to include assertion_id in auth_event and attach hashed_subject to user creation/upsert events
Extend e2e test harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/saml-test-harness PR #204 (WIP)
Confluence doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SSEC/pages/IdP+Attribute+Harmonization updated with playbook and support snippets
